paper.title: HumanoidMimicGen: Data Generation for Loco-Manipulation via Whole-Body Planning

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Direct humanoid loco-manipulation data-generation and policy-learning study with simulation and real evaluation.

sections_read.purpose: Inspect skill planning, retargeting and data generation.
Verify policy results across nine tasks.

research_question: Can one human demonstration be expanded into enough feasible whole-body data to train humanoid loco-manipulation policies?
contributions: A skill-structured generation pipeline and a nine-task loco-manipulation benchmark.

method.summary: Human demonstrations are segmented into skills, retargeted through a hybrid action space, randomized and rolled out with whole-body tracking to retain successful trajectories.
assumptions: Skills and their precedence are manually specified.
Environment models and task success conditions are available.

datasets: One source human demonstration per task
study_context.sample_or_scale: Up to 1,000 successful generated trajectories per task; nine benchmark tasks.

evaluation.design: Policies trained on generated data are compared with adapted MimicGen baselines; ablations and real co-training are reported.

findings.finding: Skill-aware data generation from one source demonstration substantially improved average learned-policy performance over the strongest adapted baseline.
findings.scope: Nine simulated benchmark tasks with a fixed skill graph per task.

author_stated.limitation: The system requires manual skill and precedence annotations, environment setup and success conditions, and uses fixed skill sequences and rigid transforms.

reader_inferred.boundary: The generation gain does not remove task-engineering costs.
reader_inferred.basis: The limitation section lists manual annotations, environment authoring and fixed task structure.

transfer_boundary: Best suited to known task families whose interactions can be decomposed into reusable, manually declared skills.

design_risks: Generated rollouts inherit simulator and success-detector biases.
Manual task decomposition may dominate setup effort.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: The authors adapt a strong MimicGen-style baseline to whole-body data, although all methods rely on shared environment infrastructure.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Task policy scores measure downstream utility of generated data.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Algorithm, benchmark details and raw tables are provided.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: Real results cover fewer settings than the simulation benchmark.

evidence_cards.claim: Across nine simulated tasks, data generated from one source demonstration raised average policy performance from 0.33 for DexMimicGen+ to 0.89 for HumanoidMimicGen.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports structured synthetic expansion of sparse whole-body demonstrations.
evidence_cards.summary: The main comparison reports downstream policy performance averaged over all nine tasks.
evidence_cards.source_context: From Table 1 , HumanoidMimicGen improves policy performance over all baselines in all tasks. Averaged over nine tasks, data generated by HumanoidMimicGen from a single source human demonstration increases policy performance from 0.33 (DexMimicGen+) to 0.89

verification.rationale: The paragraph explicitly states the baseline, method, nine-task average and values.
